# make_folders

[← Command index](README.md)

Move each matching file into a folder of its own, named after the file.

## Synopsis

```
make_folders [options]
```

## Description

For every file directly inside the input directory whose name ends with one of the
given extensions, creates a folder named after the file without its extension and
moves the file into it. `Game (USA).iso` becomes `Game (USA)/Game (USA).iso`.
Subdirectories and files with other extensions are left alone.

## Options

### General

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-i, --input_path <input_path>` | Directory whose top-level files are sorted into folders; it must exist. |
| `-f, --file_types <file_types>` | Comma-separated filename endings to match, with the leading dot. Default: `.iso,.chd,.rvz,.zip,.7z,.rar,.pkg`. |

### Common options

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-v, --verbose` | Enable verbose mode. |
| `-p, --pretend_run` | Do a pretend run with no permanent changes. |
| `-x, --exit_on_failure` | Enable exit on failure mode. |
| `--no-preview` | Skip the preview confirmation prompt. |

## Examples

### Put each disc image and archive in its own folder

```bash
make_folders -i ~/Roms/PS2
```

### Only handle ISO and CHD files

```bash
make_folders -i ~/Roms/PS2 -f .iso,.chd
```

### Preview the moves

```bash
make_folders -i ~/Roms/PS2 -p -v
```

## Notes

- Extensions are matched case-sensitively and must not contain spaces, so `.iso` does not match `GAME.ISO`.
- There is no confirmation prompt; use `-p -v` to see what would move first.
